text: The Patriots bid farewell to one of the franchise's greatest defensive players this week as Stephon Gilmore, the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro cornerback, signed a one-day contract to retire as a member of New England, cementing his legacy among the all-time greats in team history. On the injury front, running back TreVeyon Henderson—who missed the opener with an ankle injury—said Thursday he's "ready to go" for Sunday's Week 2 matchup against Pittsburgh, though the Patriots could be without starting cornerback Carlton Davis III, who is officially questionable heading into the contest. The team is also looking to bounce back after their season opener, facing a Steelers team that's rolling into town in strong form, setting up an intriguing divisional battle for quarterback Drake Maye and company at home. Off the field, Pro Football Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri will attempt a Guinness World Record kick at the Jungfraujoch in the Swiss Alps as part of the Patriots' promotional efforts for their upcoming game in Munich, while owner Robert Kraft explained his decision to remove Macklemore as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows, citing concerns about antisemitic rhetoric and imagery.
